title: Unusual paraneoplastic syndromes in pancreatic cancer: a case report of Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) associated with intraductal papillary mucinous cancer of the pancreas
case_prompt:
A 66-year-old Caucasian man presented in October 2021 with a recently diagnosed pancreatic head tumor. Since summer 2020 he had experienced progressive weakness and fatigue, initially in the lower extremities, making stair climbing and long walks difficult; over subsequent months, weakness extended to proximal upper extremities, accompanied by dysphonia and dysarthria. He also reported decreased appetite and a 30-kg weight loss over the past year. His medical history was notable only for a cardiac pacemaker implanted for arrhythmia. 

Contrast CT of the abdomen revealed a 3-cm cystic lesion in the pancreatic head. Laboratory tests showed a CA19-9 level of 341 U/mL (normal <27) and a CEA level of 6.5 ng/mL (normal <5). In October 2021, he underwent a Whipple procedure; histopathology demonstrated a poorly differentiated pancreatic adenocarcinoma arising in an intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (staged pT3 N2 M0, Grade 3).

Postoperatively, he failed to resume spontaneous breathing and showed generalized areflexia. Train-of-four monitoring of the ulnar nerve (2 Hz stimulation) demonstrated a 60% decrement in the fourth twitch. Myasthenia gravis and Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome were considered. He was started on pyridostigmine 90 mg daily, which led to sufficient improvement for extubation and transfer. 

On the ward, he developed diplopia, dysarthria, diffuse areflexia, and paraparesis of the lower limbs. Neurological examination revealed strength (Medical Research Council scale) of 4/5 in shoulder girdle muscles, 5/5 in wrist movements, 3/5 in hip flexion, 4/5 in knee movements, and 4/5 in ankle movements; spinal reflexes were absent throughout, and sensory examination was normal.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Myasthenia gravis was considered but excluded — “Acetylcholine receptor binding and ganglionic neuronal antibodies were undetected.”  
2. Myositis was ruled out — “Creatin kinase (CK) levels were normal.”  
3. Small-cell lung cancer as the source of paraneoplastic syndrome was excluded — “A further diagnosis with CT scan of thorax excluded a lung tumor.”  
4. Other paraneoplastic and autoimmune neuromuscular antibodies were negative — “immunological laboratory tests of anti-SOX-1, titin, anti-LRP4 IgG … did not manifest any abnormalities.”  
5. LEMS was confirmed by the presence of characteristic antibodies — “Serum paraneoplastic work-up was positive for P/Q-type calcium channel antibodies (381.1 pmol/L; range, <40 pmol/L).”
